Use case: stylized-concept. Produce a precise axial modeling reference of ONE Rail Arena character.
INPUT ROLES: Image 1 is a headless Blender TRUE TOP orthographic camera/occlusion GUIDE. Image 2 is its TRUE BOTTOM orthographic camera/occlusion GUIDE. Their old rough modeling and flat materials are NOT the desired art style. Image 3 is the approved-direction TURNAROUND, the identity, costume and silhouette authority. Image 4 is the matching DETAILS sheet, the hair/armor/glove and boot/sole construction authority.
Make ONE LANDSCAPE sheet with two broad horizontal rows: TOP ORTHOGRAPHIC above, BOTTOM ORTHOGRAPHIC below. Each row contains the complete character projected exactly along the standing vertical axis, following the camera and physical occlusion in guide 1/2. Light gray background, neutral studio shading, high-quality polished low-poly game art EXACTLY matching images 3/4.
CRITICAL: match the compact wide horizontal projection shape of the GUIDES. There is no visible standing height in these views. Do not tilt the camera to reveal a face, torso front, long thighs or long shins. Do not spread the hands forward toward the camera or bend the elbows. Keep the straight neutral A-pose from the turnaround, projected vertically: shoulders/arms spread horizontally across the image, two hands at outer ends, head/collar and small toe tips in TOP, two short complete soles and palm undersides in BOTTOM. The waist/legs are hidden where the head/shoulders or soles physically occlude them. No frontal standing figures, no 3/4 portraits, no distant feet or perspective foreshortening. All limbs, hair and feet must be within the row with comfortable margin.
Improve only the rough GUIDES' appearance to the exact sophisticated sculpted hair, beveled shoulder shells, suited fabric, forearm bracers, fingerless gloves and fitted boot design in images 3/4. Do not copy the crude guide's nose/eyelids, disconnected shapes, shoulder interiors, blank outsole, or old clothing mistakes. The head from TOP is its actual directional hair crown with only tiny protruding nose/ear tips if physically exposed; never eyes or a full face. Make closed armor shells, not hollow tubes. The bottom view shows the accurate tread design from the corresponding boot SOLE detail card in image 4, not a new invented universal tread pattern.
Anatomical side invariant: TOP camera projects character RIGHT on viewer LEFT. BOTTOM camera projects character RIGHT on viewer RIGHT. Front/toe direction points DOWN the sheet in BOTH rows. Do not mirror asymmetric equipment when changing the camera. The bottoms of the soles must point in the same front/toe direction, retaining real toe and heel shapes and the detail sheet's tread. Small R and L tags at horizontal ends of each row may clarify the anatomical sides.
This is a true top/bottom counterpart to the supplied eight-angle turnaround, not a new costume design. Labels: character title, TOP ORTHOGRAPHIC, BOTTOM ORTHOGRAPHIC only, plus the small R/L tags. Do not add slogans, dimensions or extra diagrams.
Image 5, if provided, is a corrected PLAYER AXIAL sheet used ONLY as the two-row layout and projection guide. Do not transfer his hair, face, ivory/cyan costume or extra plates to this character. Use this character's exact colors and equipment from images 3/4.
TOP shoulder shells must be CLOSED colored armor caps, as in the character's own turnaround/detail, never the rough guide's huge black void interiors. BOTTOM gloves must show padded PALMS without back-of-hand knuckle plates. BOTTOM anatomical tags: L on viewer LEFT, R on viewer RIGHT. TOP tags: R viewer LEFT, L viewer RIGHT. BOTTOM soles must have their BROAD ROUNDED TOE ENDS at the LOWER edge of the sheet, their narrower HEELS at the UPPER edge. Rotate the existing tread card 180 degrees if needed to preserve this toe-down convention; do not invent a different tread pattern.
guideOnlyRole: orthographic camera direction and occlusion; old mesh appearances are not approved design authority
appearanceInputs: Each character's selected Turnaround and Details PNGs

corrections.Player:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this PLAYER axial reference sheet, preserving the true compact wide top/bottom projection, exact identity/costume palette, straight A-pose, layout, and all other details. Fix these specific mistakes:
TOP row: the two large black void-like areas on top of the shoulders wrongly copy the old rough guide. Replace those inner/top shoulder areas with the player's CLOSED beveled ivory armor crown shells, with narrow charcoal joint seams at the inner edge, consistent with the shoulder plates in the attached second image (player detail sheet). They must be solid shaped ivory/champagne upper shoulder shells, not hollow tubes or giant black pads. Keep the correct camera view straight down, hair crown and gloves in position.
BOTTOM row: switch side tags so LEFT image end reads L and RIGHT image end reads R (true underside anatomical sides). TOP row R left / L right is already correct.
BOTTOM row: rotate the entire appearance/outline/tread of BOTH boot sole views EXACTLY 180 degrees IN THEIR OWN PLACES, so their broad rounded TOE ends point DOWN the sheet and narrow HEEL ends point UP. Keep soles the same size and position and use the tread from the attached boot sole detail card, with all parts rotated together. Do not leave toe-up soles. Do not rotate the whole body or row.
BOTTOM row: replace back-of-hand knuckle plates with the actual PALM surfaces from the attached right-glove PALM detail: dark padded palm panels, fingerless tips, no silver back-of-hand plates on the palms. Keep hands in the same physically projected positions.
Do not introduce any visible face, long standing torso/legs, perspective tilt, extra armor, new motifs, or crop the outer fingers. Keep all labels legible and this same two-row composition.
corrections.Bot01:
Use case: precise-object-edit. This is the Bot01 axial sheet. Preserve both complete body projections, costume, colors, face occlusion, pose, labels and all other artwork. Modify ONLY the TWO BOOT SOLES in the BOTTOM ROW and the tiny yellow V below the hair in TOP ROW.
Each sole is currently TOE-UP, which is opposite to this camera's front/toe-DOWN convention. Treat each sole as a flat picture and rotate it IN PLACE exactly HALF A TURN (180 degrees) without moving its center. To make this unmistakable: the big orange Y-shaped tread motif must become UPSIDE-DOWN: its two fork arms must branch DOWNWARD toward the lower edge, and its single long stem must point UPWARD toward the top edge. The broad rounded forefoot must be at the BOTTOM of each sole patch; the narrow heel pad must be at the TOP. All tread polygons and colored insets must rotate with the sole; no new tread or costume. Use the exact same orange Y tread just rotated, not a freshly drawn toe-up sole. Both soles' centers, total size and mounting positions are unchanged.
Top row: remove the tiny bright yellow V-shaped point directly below the nose/hair near the center-front chest edge; replace it with plain terracotta/dark charcoal seam consistent with her chest reference. Do not alter amber collar piping or any other amber accents.
Do not rotate hands, body, background or text. The bottom palms and L-left/R-right labels are already correct.
corrections.Bot02:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit only the TWO SOLE TREAD SURFACES in the BOTTOM ROW of this Bot02 axial sheet. Image 2 is the Bot02 detail sheet: its boot SOLE card (bottom row column 2, right-hand sole) is the tread/material authority. The axial sheet mistakenly copied the PLAYER's ivory X-like sole inserts around the teal middle recess.
Remove every ivory/champagne colored patch FROM THE SOLE TREAD SURFACES ONLY, replacing those exact tread areas with matching dark charcoal rubber as in the Bot02 sole card. Keep the teal outlined hexagonal central shank recess and small teal heel dash, and retain the existing dark geometric tread pattern. The small heel dash must remain at TOP (heel), broader forefoot at BOTTOM (toe). Do not recolor the pale boot SIDE RIMS outside the sole or any shoulder/forearm armor. Preserve all other body artwork, hair, camera view, scale, labels, palettes, gloves and pose exactly. The Bot02 sole should be dark rubber plus a teal outlined recess and tiny teal dash, NOT the player's ivory/cyan X-shape.
corrections.Bot03:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Keep this Bot03 axial sheet unchanged except for the TWO BOOT SOLE PATCHES in the bottom row. They are currently oriented toe-UP, opposite to the required front/toe-DOWN convention.
Rotate EACH entire sole view exactly 180 degrees IN PLACE around its own center, including its outline, every tread polygon and the central copper shank pad. The asymmetric tiny BLACK FASTENER DOT in the copper center pad is now near the BOTTOM tip of that pad; after this half-turn it MUST be near the TOP tip of the copper pad. That is the key visible check that the sole actually rotated. The forefoot's broad rounded toe must now be at BOTTOM, narrow heel at TOP. Keep both soles the same total size and mounted centers; do not change the tread design, create a new symmetric pattern, or recolor it.
Do not rotate the rest of the body, hands, background, words, labels or top view. Preserve the top-view right-swept locs and left cropped temple, deep skin, plum/copper armor and all camera/pose geometry. Bottom palms and the L-left/R-right side labels are already correct.

limitations: Guided concept reconstructions, not calibrated final shared-mesh projections.
